title: Sleep when you're dead
subtitle: for the figures who never stop working
narrative: The card art is honest about who pays. The mind eaten alive by parasitic demands. The servant scrubbing greatness's floor. The tax-collector knocking with armed escort. The vow-monks with their mouths stitched shut so they don't ruin the ceremony. The vampire pontiff blessing the extraction. The lawmage in marble robes locking a captive into restraints. Most TCG art treats labor as backdrop ornament, ambient unfreedom you're meant to look past. This bundle puts the backdrop in the foreground. Six cards. Six people working past the point you'd say sleep, if anyone was asking.

cards.name: Mind Rot
cards.why_it_fits: Steve Luke's Welcome Deck 2016 art (reprinted via The List in Mystery Booster). A figure screaming as vines and parasitic growths erupt from their skull. The labor register here is body-horror, what burnout looks like when rendered as physiology. The parasitic growths are the deadlines that won't stop arriving. Anchor card.

cards.name: Wicked Guardian
cards.why_it_fits: Flavor text reads: "Some are born to greatness. You were born to scrub greatness's floors." The noble stands; the servant scrubs. The art renders class violence as house cleaning. Counter-anchor card.

cards.name: Charity Extractor
cards.why_it_fits: Two fully-armored knights with polearms, faces hidden under plate. The card title says it all. "Extracting charity" is the medieval euphemism for armed taxation. The labor here is the obligation, not the depicted figures.

cards.name: Deafening Silence
cards.why_it_fits: Three robed monks with their mouths literally stitched shut. The labor is consent under duress, a vow that punishes the body for speaking. Reads as ambient horror at first, as institutional discipline on second look.

cards.name: Lawmage's Binding
cards.why_it_fits: Two Azorius lawmages binding a horned figure with chains of magic. The carceral apparatus made concrete. Where Crush Dissent (last draft) gave you the boot in abstract, this card shows the cuffs, the runes, the marble robes, the two-person team that does the holding. Labor under coercion gets a face when the coercer also has a face.

cards.name: Pitiless Pontiff
cards.why_it_fits: Vampire cleric in a gold mask with a blade. The Orzhov frame. Priesthood as extraction made literal: the church is also the bank, and the rites are also the receipts. Labor's spiritual face when the spiritual face is the same face as the landlord's.

pricing.diy_alternative_note: Assumes 2 to 3 TCGplayer sellers covering the list at plain-envelope rates. Realistic floor; could be higher if cards spread across more sellers.
pricing.shipping_policy: buyer-paid, itemized separately at checkout; never included in list price
pricing.premium_justification: The $1.24 above cost basis pays for the writing, the framing, the thesis. The buyer is not buying $3.16 of cards. They're buying a zine with cards stapled in.

metadata.notes: Second draft. Replaced Discordant Piper and Crush Dissent with Lawmage's Binding and Pitiless Pontiff for tighter Labor-hub fit. Used the BBL graph (cards/_hubs/labor.md tag_signals + corpus query) to find candidates.
